code: H5O__chunk_deserialize(udata->oh, udata->common.addr, udata->size, (const uint8_t *)image, len, &(udata->common), dirty)
note: The continuation chunk is loaded with udata->size set to the attacker-controlled cont->size, which is passed as chunk_size to H5O__chunk_deserialize.
For continuation chunks (chunkno > 0), the chunk size is set directly to the attacker-controlled chunk_size without any minimum validation.
A heap buffer of the attacker-controlled small size is allocated for the chunk image.
The check only verifies len >= chunk_size, but len is the actual disk image length which can be larger than the allocated buffer size.
Copies exactly chunk_size bytes into the allocated buffer - this is safe, but the buffer is undersized for the subsequent checksum verification.
When chunk_size is less than H5O_SIZEOF_CHKSUM_OH (4 bytes), the subtraction underflows, producing a pointer before the start of the buffer.
The loop condition compares against the underflowed eom_ptr, causing out-of-bounds reads from the undersized heap buffer.
The out-of-bounds read can trigger a heap-buffer-overflow when decoding message data from beyond the allocated chunk buffer, leading to a crash.
